title: bomify plugin SecurityResult
description: The single JSON object a bomify-plugin-<type> binary must print to stdout on success for its "security scan" subcommand, per plugins/SECURITY-CONTRACT.md. "vulnerabilities" is every regular CycloneDX vulnerability object (see https://cyclonedx.org/docs/ for its full schema, not re-specified here) describing something the scanned --purl is affected by. "components" is optional: every regular CycloneDX component the plugin found while unpacking the scanned --purl into smaller pieces to scan it at all (e.g. cataloging a container image's contents) - bomify embeds them as that component's own nested components. Validate a plugin's actual stdout output (one line, one object) against this schema to check it for structural conformance; it only constrains the bomify-specific parts (the object wrapper, and that each vulnerability's affects is the plugin's own responsibility to set), not every CycloneDX field.

bom-ref.description: A stable identifier for this vulnerability (the vulnerability's own id is a reasonable choice). bomify merges two components' results that report the same bom-ref into a single entry, combining their affects — a vulnerability with no bom-ref is never merged with another.

id.description: The vulnerability's own identifier, e.g. a CVE or GHSA id.

affects.description: Set by the plugin, not bomify. For a purl scanned directly (no "components" reported), a single entry referencing that same purl string back. For a purl unpacked into pieces ("components" is non-empty), one entry per affected piece, referencing its bom-ref from "components" - never the top-level purl itself.

components.description: Optional. Every piece the plugin found while unpacking the scanned --purl to scan it at all (e.g. the packages found by cataloging a container image). Omit entirely, or leave empty, if the plugin scanned the purl directly. bomify embeds this list as the scanned component's own nested components in the SBOM.

bom-ref.description: A stable identifier for this piece (a purl, if it has one, is a reasonable choice) - this is what a vulnerability's affects[].ref should point at when this piece is the one actually affected.
